Hormonaly Academy · Hormones and Peptides for Skin · stage 60 media · human media preview

Media preview — opening films and teaching stills

One explanatory still for each narrated moment (48 in all). Each one sits above the play control on the audio card, so on a phone the learner sees it while the narration plays. Every still is a draft: nothing is approved until Omar Saleem signs off the design and Dr. Fady Hannah-Shmouni signs off the scientific accuracy. All words stay in the app (titles, chapters, alt text); the pictures carry no text, numbers, doses, products or faces.

Look at first15moments with a scientific point to confirm

How to review

  • Scientific accuracy (Dr. Hannah-Shmouni): does the picture show what the moment says, at the level it is drawn? A wrong figure is worse than none — mark any still to redraw or drop.
  • Design (Omar): one set, one hand; calm paper register; the violet marks the one thing the moment is about.
  • Phone view: on a phone the play control covers roughly the bottom quarter of the picture.
  • Reply with the moment id (for example m5-p14) and "keep", "redraw: …" or "drop".

Look at these first

  • m5-p14 A Wnt switch and a zinc question. — Most complex mechanism in the set: a cell-penetrating decoy peptide sits in the docking site so the grey 'brake' protein (CXXC5) cannot bind Dishevelled, and β-catenin tokens move into the nucleus. Confirm this reading of PTD-DBM (Lee 2017).
  • m3-p08 Two gut hormones, re-engineered. — DPP-4 drawn clipping the two N-terminal residues off native GLP-1; the drug drawn with a substituted second residue and a fatty side chain. Confirm this is acceptable for semaglutide and tirzepatide at this level of detail.
  • m2-p17 Freckles before the wedding. — Pedigree shows an affected father and daughter (mother unaffected). Redrawn at review: the myxoma now sits in the left atrium (the upper chamber on the viewer's right of a textbook four-chamber cutaway, beside the pulmonary-vein openings), the commoner site; it is drawn as a small stalked mass by the septum reaching toward the mitral valve.
  • m4-p03 A plasma tripeptide with a copper habit. — GHK-Cu drawn as three beads with the copper ion against the first two (Gly-His). Schematic only; confirm.
  • m5-p07 Five receptors, one family of hormones. — Five receptor tiles: MC1R pigment cell, MC2R adrenal, MC3R and MC4R brain (drawn twice), MC5R sebaceous gland — the tidy map the moment itself qualifies.
  • m7-p02 GRADE rates certainty in an effect, one outcome at a time. — GRADE: randomized trials on the top shelf, observational studies on the third; the model also put a small cluster on the lowest shelf (very low). Keep, or redraw with the lowest shelf empty?
  • m6-p05 Deficiency is a diagnosis. Decline is ageing. — Deficiency drawn as a pituitary mass (one cause among several); normal ageing drawn as an intact gland releasing less.
  • m3-p13 Ten months in, and unhappy with the mirror. — Facial fat drawn as one pad over bone; real anatomy has separate superficial and deep compartments.
  • m1-p06 Read the skin before the serum. — Skin sign paired with gland: thin skin with bruising and the adrenal (cortisol excess); coarse dry skin and the thyroid; acanthosis nigricans and the pancreas (hyperinsulinaemia).
  • m6-p17 Tight rings, eight months into 'CJC/ipa'. — Tingling drawn along the thumb, index and middle fingers (median nerve) to match carpal tunnel symptoms.
  • m4-p13 Rodents, a fragment, and a tripeptide. — TB-500 drawn as a seven-bead fragment lifted from the first half of a long chain (residues 17–23 of thymosin β4); KPV as the last three beads of α-MSH.
  • m5-p05 Work up the hair loss before anyone mentions a peptide. — Four hair-loss patterns seen from above: male pattern, diffuse shedding, an alopecia areata patch, female-pattern widened parting. The front of three ovals is bare (forehead).
  • m2-p13 Some syndromes show on the skin first. — Only the MEN2A example is drawn: interscapular cutaneous lichen amyloidosis linked to the thyroid.
  • m2-p11 Symptoms and bone. Skin is a bystander. — Two of the approved uses drawn (vasomotor symptoms, bone); vulvovaginal symptoms are left to the text.
  • m2-p15 The everyday endocrine signs. — Three of the named signs drawn: palm creases (adrenal), acanthosis nigricans at the back of the neck, a pretibial plaque; hirsutism and hypothyroid skin are left to the text.

Module 01The skin as an endocrine organ, and how it ages

m1-p03 · 03 / 19 · Lesson 1.1 · Concept

Four units, one circuit.

Lesson 1.1 · The skin as a steroidogenic, endocrine organ

Teaches
Skin as a neuro-immuno-endocrine organ: four units, three signalling routes (neighbouring cells, nerves, blood); mostly cell, tissue and animal evidence.
Alt text
A cross-section of skin showing the epidermis, dermis, fat layer and a hair follicle with its glands, with signals passing between cells, along a nerve and into a blood vessel.

Regenerated 2 times — style anchor, first candidate sat too low in the frame for the phone pane (house composition line tightened); then second candidate still too low (composition line tightened again)

m1-p06 · 06 / 19 · What changes in practice

Read the skin before the serum.

Lesson 1.1 · The skin as a steroidogenic, endocrine organ

Teaches
The aesthetic exam as a systemic screen: thinning and bruising, coarse dry skin and acanthosis nigricans point to cortisol, thyroid and insulin; some signs mean prompt referral.
Alt text
Three magnified patches of skin — thin with a bruise, coarse and dry, velvety and dark — each linked to the gland it points to: an adrenal gland, the thyroid and the pancreas.

Check firstSkin sign paired with gland: thin skin with bruising and the adrenal (cortisol excess); coarse dry skin and the thyroid; acanthosis nigricans and the pancreas (hyperinsulinaemia).

Regenerated 1 time — wrong sign-to-gland wiring (bruise->thyroid, dry->adrenal); glands low in frame

assets/hormones-peptides-skin/images/m1-p06-img.jpg · gemini-3.1-flash-image · draft · 2026-09-25

m1-p08 · 08 / 19 · Lesson 1.2 · Concept

A map of fourteen million cells.

Lesson 1.2 · The Hormone Cell Atlas: receptor maps and what they prove

Teaches
The Hormone Cell Atlas read hormone and receptor RNA cell by cell across human tissues: a map of predicted capacity, not measured hormone release.
Alt text
A grid of small tissue tiles with a skin tile at the centre, where some cells carry receptor cups and a few hold outlined granules, marking cells predicted to respond to or make a hormone.

assets/hormones-peptides-skin/images/m1-p08-img.jpg · gemini-3.1-flash-image · draft · 2026-09-25

m1-p11 · 11 / 19 · What changes in practice

A map to confirm, then a trial.

Lesson 1.2 · The Hormone Cell Atlas: receptor maps and what they prove

Teaches
A receptor on a map is where an efficacy question starts; skin enzymes change potency; only a human trial answers it (sunscreen and vitamin D as the example).
Alt text
A droplet on the skin reaches a cell's receptor while an enzyme reshapes a passing molecule, and a line leads to two matched groups of dots standing for a randomized trial.

Regenerated 1 time — trial motif rendered as stacked coins (reads as money)

assets/hormones-peptides-skin/images/m1-p11-img.jpg · gemini-3.1-flash-image · draft · 2026-09-25

m1-p13 · 13 / 19 · Lesson 1.3 · Concept

Cells that stop dividing and keep talking.

Lesson 1.3 · Senescence, the SASP and the ageing dermis

Teaches
Senescent cells stop dividing but keep secreting cytokines, enzymes and growth factors (the SASP); p16-positive cells become more common with age in human skin.
Alt text
On the left a cell divides into two; on the right a larger, flattened cell has stopped dividing and releases a cloud of small particles into the frayed fibres around it.

assets/hormones-peptides-skin/images/m1-p13-img.jpg · gemini-3.1-flash-image · draft · 2026-09-25

m1-p16 · 16 / 19 · Where the evidence is strongest

The levers with trials behind them.

Lesson 1.3 · Senescence, the SASP and the ageing dermis

Teaches
The levers with randomized trials: daily sunscreen (B) and topical retinoids (tretinoin, guide A; retinol C); senotherapies are biomarker pilots.
Alt text
A skin cross-section with a thin protective film turning back sun rays and a few drops soaking in, above dense, orderly collagen in the dermis.

assets/hormones-peptides-skin/images/m1-p16-img.jpg · gemini-3.1-flash-image · draft · 2026-09-25

m1-p17 · 17 / 19 · Fictional case

'Can a senolytic fix my skin?'

Lesson 1.3 · Senescence, the SASP and the ageing dermis

Teaches
Fictional case: senolytic supplements rest on mouse data and small human pilots; daily sunscreen and topical retinoids have randomized trials with visible outcomes.
Alt text
Three steps of evidence, from a culture dish to a mouse to a human trial; an unmarked capsule sits on the mouse step, while a sun-protection film sits on the top step.

Module 02Systemic hormones and the skin

m2-p02 · 02 / 19 · Mechanism

The skin regenerates its own cortisol.

Lesson 2.1 · Cortisol signatures: local 11β-HSD1 and Cushing's syndrome

Teaches
Skin regenerates cortisol from cortisone with 11β-HSD1, more with age and sun exposure; cortisol slows collagen synthesis; visible ageing in people is untested.
Alt text
A magnified skin cell in which an enzyme turns an inactive hormone into its active form, surrounded by thin, sparse collagen fibres.

Regenerated 1 time — copied the anchor's follicle/nerve/vessel, key-shaped tokens, no sparse collagen

m2-p06 · 06 / 19 · What changes in practice

Reassure the many, refer the few.

Lesson 2.1 · Cortisol signatures: local 11β-HSD1 and Cushing's syndrome

Teaches
'Cortisol face': take the glucocorticoid history, look for discriminating features, reassure most, and route the few to formal testing and an endocrinologist.
Alt text
A stream of tokens passes under a lens; most continue into a calm pool, while a few violet tokens turn onto a path toward a small building.

m2-p08 · 08 / 19 · Lesson 2.2 · Concept

Estrogen and the dermis.

Lesson 2.2 · Estrogen, menopause and dermal collagen

Teaches
Estrogen receptors sit in all skin; topical estradiol raised collagen in sun-protected but not photoaged skin; skin collagen falls with years since menopause.
Alt text
Two panels of dermis: in sun-protected skin, receptor-bearing cells lay down new collagen; in sun-damaged skin, the same cells sit among fragmented, clumped fibres with no new collagen.

Regenerated 1 time — anchor's violet nerve and vessel copied into both panels — violet in the photoaged panel reads as new collagen

m2-p11 · 11 / 19 · Regulatory status and indications

Symptoms and bone. Skin is a bystander.

Lesson 2.2 · Estrogen, menopause and dermal collagen

Teaches
US and UK menopausal hormone therapy is approved for symptoms and bone protection; the 2025–26 US label changes did not add skin; compounded 'bioidentical' products lack data.
Alt text
An open frame holds rising heat lines and a piece of spongy bone, while a small block of skin sits outside it, drawn in grey.

Some syndromes show on the skin first.

Teaches
Some inherited endocrine syndromes show on the skin first: MEN1 angiofibromas, Carney complex lentigines and myxomas, MEN2A lichen amyloidosis before thyroid cancer.
Alt text
An upper back seen from behind with a rippled, pigmented patch between the shoulder blades, linked by a fine line to a drawing of the thyroid gland.

The everyday endocrine signs.

Everyday endocrine signs: adrenal darkening in creases, fast or virilising hirsutism, acanthosis nigricans, pretibial myxoedema, cold dry hypothyroid skin.

Three body-part outlines with typical sites marked: the palm creases, a velvety patch at the back of the neck, and a raised plaque on the front of the shin.

Teaches

Module 03Fat, incretins and the ageing face

m3-p02 · 02 / 20 · Mechanism

The skin keeps its own fat.

Lesson 3.1 · Dermal fat and matrix glycation

Teaches
Dermal white adipose tissue: a fat layer inside the dermis, in cones around follicles in humans; antimicrobial in mice; its part in human skin ageing is unmeasured.
Alt text
A skin cross-section in which a cone of small fat cells surrounds the lower hair follicle inside the dermis, separate from the fat layer beneath.

Regenerated 2 times — anchor arcs/nerve copied in violet, pink surface line (second hue); then cone beside, not around, the follicle

assets/hormones-peptides-skin/images/m3-p02-img.jpg · gemini-3.1-flash-image · draft · 2026-09-25

m3-p04 · 04 / 20 · Mechanism

Sugar that sticks to collagen.

Lesson 3.1 · Dermal fat and matrix glycation

Teaches
Glycation: sugars bind collagen and end as AGEs that cross-link and stiffen the matrix; RAGE signalling in lab studies; the causal link to visible ageing is graded D.
Alt text
On the left, parallel collagen fibres lie free; on the right, the same fibres carry small sugar rings and are tied together by short cross-links.

Regenerated 1 time — atom letter 'O' drawn inside each sugar ring (text in pixels)

assets/hormones-peptides-skin/images/m3-p04-img.jpg · gemini-3.1-flash-image · draft · 2026-09-25

m3-p08 · 08 / 20 · Lesson 3.2 · Concept

Two gut hormones, re-engineered.

Lesson 3.2 · Incretin therapy and the changing face

Teaches
GLP-1 and GIP are incretins; native GLP-1 is cleared within minutes by DPP-4; semaglutide and tirzepatide are engineered to last, for approved indications.
Alt text
On the left an enzyme clips a pair of units off the end of a natural hormone chain; on the right a modified chain with an altered unit and a fatty tail resists the enzyme and stays whole.

Check firstDPP-4 drawn clipping the two N-terminal residues off native GLP-1; the drug drawn with a substituted second residue and a fatty side chain. Confirm this is acceptable for semaglutide and tirzepatide at this level of detail.

Regenerated 2 times — enzyme cut the chain mid-way instead of removing the two end residues; then three beads clipped instead of two (DPP-4 removes a dipeptide)

Counsel before, record during, refer when asked.

Lesson 3.2 · Incretin therapy and the changing face

Teaches
On GLP-1 drugs: counsel before treatment, photograph with consent during, refer restoration requests; restoration advice is expert opinion.

A path passes two blank conversation cards, a camera pointed at a blank frame, and an open door into another room.

Lesson 3.2 · Incretin therapy and the changing face

Teaches
Fictional case: facial volume loss and shedding on an effective, approved GLP-1 drug — counsel, record and refer; whether to stop belongs with her prescriber.

Two cross-sections of cheek tissue over bone: one with a full fat pad under the skin, the other with a thinner pad and looser skin above it.

m3-p15 · 15 / 20 · Lesson 3.3 · Concept

Inflammation that comes with age.

Lesson 3.3 · Gut barrier, endotoxaemia and inflammaging

Teaches
Inflammaging and the gut hypothesis: bacterial LPS crossing a leaky barrier, shown in mice and briefly after a fatty meal; not shown to drive skin disease.

Two views of the gut lining: one with closed junctions keeping small bacterial fragments out, the other with loosened junctions letting them pass into a blood vessel.

Diet first, a bottle last.

Lesson 3.3 · Gut barrier, endotoxaemia and inflammaging

Teaches
Gut and skin: diet quality, metabolic care and established skin treatment come first; a zonulin test cannot show a leaky gut; gut-repair peptides last, if at all.

A row of stepping stones leads from a plate of whole foods, past a small block of skin, to a single unmarked capsule on the last, smallest stone.

A plasma tripeptide with a copper habit.

Teaches
GHK-Cu: a plasma tripeptide that binds copper; the proposed copper-delivery and gene-expression mechanism comes largely from its discoverer's group.

A three-bead peptide holds a copper ion, with fine lines toward the collagen fibres and enzymes it is proposed to supply.

m4-p06 · 06 / 19 · What changes in practice

Serum yes, syringe no.

Lesson 4.1 · Copper peptides: GHK and GHK-Cu

Teaches
Topical GHK-Cu is a reasonable cosmetic conversation (C); injected GHK-Cu has no trials, irritates tissue, and in the US sits outside the Category 1 listing.
Alt text
Two skin cross-sections: drops resting on the surface on the left, and a deposit deep in the dermis with a ring of irritated tissue on the right.

m4-p08 · 08 / 19 · Lesson 4.2 · Concept

Three families, one question: who ran the trial?

Lesson 4.2 · Signal peptides, oral collagen and SNAP-25 mimics

Teaches
Three families — signal peptides, SNAP-25 mimics, oral collagen — all have trial records; the question that matters most is who funded them.
Alt text
Three vignettes: a fatty-tailed peptide near a skin fibroblast, a peptide at a nerve-muscle junction, and a collagen chain breaking into small pieces in the gut.

m4-p11 · 11 / 19 · What changes in practice

Cosmetic, supplement, drug: three rulebooks.

Lesson 4.2 · Signal peptides, oral collagen and SNAP-25 mimics

Teaches
Cosmetic, supplement, drug: in the US and UK, cosmetic peptides and oral collagen reach sale without proving efficacy; only drugs pass an approval gate.
Alt text
Three lanes: a droplet and a capsule pass freely, while a tablet waits at a violet barrier across the third lane.

Regenerated 2 times — gates overlapped the supplement lane (implies supplements face approval); then violet gate still spanned the supplement lane

m4-p13 · 13 / 19 · Lesson 4.3 · Concept

Rodents, a fragment, and a tripeptide.

Lesson 4.3 · Repair peptides and the compounding line

Teaches
BPC-157 rests on rodent studies and case series; TB-500 is a seven-residue fragment of thymosin β4, never trialled; KPV is α-MSH's end tripeptide with no human RCT.
Alt text

Module 05Follicle, pigment and melanocortins

m5-p02 · 02 / 19 · Mechanism

A follicle that runs its own hormones.

Lesson 5.1 · The hair follicle as an endocrine mini-organ

Teaches
The follicle runs its own stress axis and GH/IGF-1 loop; local DHT drives pattern hair loss; alopecia areata follows the collapse of immune privilege.

A hair follicle with a closed feedback loop drawn around its bulb, which sits inside a faint protective shell that keeps nearby immune cells out.

Module 06The growth-hormone axis and the skin

m6-p02 · 02 / 19 · Lesson 6.1 · Mechanism

Two hormones, two layers of skin.

Lesson 6.1 · Growth hormone and IGF-1 in skin homeostasis

Teaches
GH acts mainly on dermal fibroblasts; fibroblast-made IGF-1 drives keratinocytes to divide; GH and IGF-1 fall steadily with age (the somatopause).
Alt text
A skin cross-section where growth hormone from a capillary reaches fibroblasts in the dermis, which send smaller signals up to dividing cells at the base of the epidermis.

m6-p05 · 05 / 19 · What changes in practice

Deficiency is a diagnosis. Decline is ageing.

Lesson 6.1 · Growth hormone and IGF-1 in skin homeostasis

Teaches
GH deficiency is a diagnosis; the fall with age is not. In healthy older adults GH brings small body-composition shifts and more side effects; distributing it for anti-ageing is a US federal offence.
Alt text
Two views of the pituitary: one pressed by a mass and releasing nothing, the other intact but releasing only a few small droplets.

Check firstDeficiency drawn as a pituitary mass (one cause among several); normal ageing drawn as an intact gland releasing less.

US compounding: 503A is patient-specific, with a strict order for bulk substances (monograph, approved-drug component, bulks list); 503B facilities are GMP-inspected; both stay unapproved.

A certificate of analysis is the supplier's report on one lot — identity by mass spectrometry, purity by HPLC — and cannot prove origin, storage or sterility.
